guide.prompt: Use case: source-subject design transfer for a reusable pet identity replacement pipeline. Image 1 is the sole authority for the replacement subject design. Copy the designated source subject's pose, action, expression, gaze, crop, silhouette rhythm, head-to-body proportion, facial abstraction, eye/nose/muzzle design, anatomical simplification, fur construction, ornament integration, line language, brushwork, pigment behavior, edge treatment, texture scale, local contrast and degree of realism. Image 2 supplies identity markers only: adult species and breed, coat colors, stable markings, ear type and eye color. Image 2 must not supply pose, expression, photographic facial construction, realistic muzzle volume, literal fur strands, lens lighting or camera depth. Create an isolated replacement-subject blueprint on a plain unobtrusive background. The replacement pet must already occupy Image 1's subject crop and reproduce Image 1's pose and expression before it enters the final scene. Do not copy the surrounding scene, text, watermark or unrelated background objects. Translate the new pet identity through Image 1's shape grammar, not through photographic anatomy. Preserve only enough breed structure to recognize the pet. Adult age means mature and healthy, not realistic: the adult pet may use the same enlarged eyes, shortened or simplified muzzle, rounded planes, graphic fur masses, mythical body treatment or painterly distortion as Image 1 without becoming a puppy or kitten. Every facial surface must be constructed from Image 1's visible marks and shapes. Replace glassy eyes, wet nose highlights, smooth three-dimensional muzzle shading, individual hair detail and photo lighting with Image 1's stylized equivalents. A face crop must read immediately as part of Image 1's artwork, never as a painted photograph of Image 2. Keep the result recognizable, appealing, adult and healthy. No generic realistic pet portrait, no studio-photo pose, no photorealistic face, no shallow depth of field, no realistic fur microtexture, no text, no logo and no watermark. Identity: adult adult German Shepherd; tan coat with defined black saddle and mask, brown eyes, tall upright ears, black muzzle and athletic adult build. Return only the finished pre-stylized identity guide.
guide.revisedPrompt: Create an isolated pre-stylized identity guide of an adult German Shepherd transformed through the shape grammar and visual language of a mythic, painterly source artwork: the dog must inherit the source image's dramatic forward-reaching pose, centered composition, intense direct gaze, enlarged heroic crop, and strong silhouette rhythm. Show the German Shepherd as mature and healthy, athletic and recognizable, with tan coat, defined black saddle and mask, black muzzle, brown eyes, and tall upright ears. Preserve only enough breed structure to read clearly as German Shepherd while translating the subject through stylized artwork, not photorealism. Use simplified facial planes, graphic muzzle construction, rounded yet strong anatomy, expressive line language, sculpted painterly fur masses instead of literal strands, and controlled edge variation. The front paw should extend toward the viewer in the same dramatic gesture as the source pose, while the head and shoulders occupy the same heroic framing. Keep the background plain, unobtrusive, and isolated with soft neutral warm-gray to pale gold tonal wash, no scenery, no text, no logo, no watermark, no props. Emphasize elegant brushwork, luminous pigment behavior, subtle edge glow, and layered tonal contrast, but avoid studio-photo realism, realistic lens effects, or shallow depth of field. The result should look like a clean identity blueprint for a reusable pet replacement pipeline: immediately readable as the same pose and energy as the source, but clearly a stylized adult German Shepherd subject.

prompt: Use case: identity-preserve precise-object-edit. Asset type: self-owned runtime frozen-master candidate. Image 1 is the current self-owned frozen master and the sole edit target. Make only the explicitly requested micro-adjustment and preserve every other visible detail, including subject identity, scene, camera, crop, pose, anatomy, costume, props, palette, lighting, depth, texture and visual medium. Keep the exact 9:16 portrait composition. No extra subjects, duplicate anatomy, malformed paws, text, logo, watermark or signature. Increase only the German Shepherd head, ears and muzzle by one subtle proportional step, approximately 10 to 12 percent, so the head fits the immense humanoid shoulders and torso naturally. The head must remain relatively small enough to preserve the monumental full-body scale, but must no longer look undersized or disconnected from the neck. Do not change the neck, shoulders, torso, extended paw, robe, body silhouette, low camera, background, lighting or framing.
revisedPrompt: Edit the provided self-owned frozen-master candidate image with extreme identity preservation and minimal change. Keep the exact same 9:16 portrait composition, camera angle, framing, pose, lighting, background, robe, body silhouette, neck, shoulders, torso, extended paw, props, palette, texture, and visual medium. Make only one subtle proportional adjustment: increase the German Shepherd head, ears, and muzzle by approximately 10–12% so the head feels naturally integrated with the immense humanoid shoulders and torso, while still remaining relatively small enough to preserve the monumental full-body scale. Do not alter anything else. No extra subjects, no duplicate anatomy, no malformed paws, no text, no logo, no watermark, no signature.
